items.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024
items.q: we co-composed it. That was for the opening of Rose Hall at Lincoln Center... my commission was settings... commissions for me and Zim

ctx.x: “Mamazala.” I got this feeling that it was a combination of church music, blues, and some classical and some South African thing in there. And I’m wondering how that particular piece came to be and if it’s a model for how you usually work?

Well everything you’ve said about it is true but it’s not a model for me because it was composed by one of my former students who was also in the Jazzanians and his name is Zim Ngqawana. And you’ll find his name on the album and in the book so you’ll be able to spell it. But you’re very correct, the kind of piano voicings in the head are just church. And that comes from the tradition Christian missionaries introduced that kind of harmony in choral singing and Africans really excel at that. Again, they’re not…
ECM as in the record label?
